definitions.explanation: A sumo wrestler who has reached the top two divisions (makuuchi or juryo). Only sekitori receive a salary and various privileges such as wearing silk mawashi.

examples.japanese: {関取|せきとり}になるのが{夢|ゆめ}だ。
examples.english: My dream is to become a ranked sumo wrestler.

examples.japanese: あの{力士|りきし}はやっと{関取|せきとり}に{昇進|しょうしん}した。
examples.english: That wrestler was finally promoted to ranked wrestler.

examples.japanese: {関取|せきとり}になると{給料|きゅうりょう}がもらえるし、{付|つ}き{人|びと}もつく。
examples.english: Once you become a ranked wrestler, you receive a salary and have personal attendants.

notes:
USAGE:
{関取|せきとり} specifically refers to wrestlers in the top two divisions ({幕内|まくうち} and {十両|じゅうりょう}). Wrestlers below these ranks are simply called {力士|りきし} (wrestler) or {取的|とりてき} (lower-ranked wrestler).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {関取|せきとり}に{昇進|しょうしん}する (to be promoted to ranked wrestler)
- {関取|せきとり}{衆|しゅう} (the ranked wrestlers collectively)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Only about 70 out of roughly 600 active sumo wrestlers hold {関取|せきとり} status at any given time. They enjoy privileges including higher pay, private rooms, and the right to wear their hair in the formal {大銀杏|おおいちょう} topknot.
